subject: Interim capacity amendment & SLA tiering — proposal and next steps
messages:
From: Alex Mendoza <alex.mendoza@skyboundlabs.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Skybound Labs Procurement <procurement@skyboundlabs.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-term pool adjustment & renewal questions

Hi Soojin,

Hope you9re well. We9re planning to accelerate rollout of our new multimodal feature in Q3 and are looking at two changes to our Dedicated pool before the next renewal:

- Add capacity mid-contract (we9re considering +50% GPUs for 3 months) vs. amending our commit for the remainder of the contract term
- Confirm how throughput guarantees scale with added GPUs (we need p95 latency assurances for 8k tokens concurrent workload)
- Understand pricing impact (pro-rated charges, discount recomputation if we amend the reserved commit)

Can you send a short runbook of options and a ballpark quote? Also attaching our traffic profile for the past 30 days (see procurement CC).

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Mendoza
Director, Product Engineering | Skybound Labs
alex.mendoza@skyboundlabs.com

Attachment: skybound_traffic_profile_May2027.csv (text/csv)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mendoza <alex.mendoza@skyboundlabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Skybound Labs Procurement <procurement@skyboundlabs.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-term pool adjustment & renewal questions

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the note and the traffic profile. High level options so we can align quickly:

1) Top-up (burst) add: temporary +32 GPUs for 3 months as a burst pool. No committed pricing change; billed at burst rate (higher unit price). Fastest to provision, but no change to long-term discount.

2) Amendment (preferred for capacity guarantee): amend reserved commit to increase pool from 64 -> 96 GPUs for the remaining contract term (12 months). This would reprofile pricing; we can offer a deeper tiered discount on the uplift vs the one-off burst. Pro-rated billing for the uplift month.

Tradeoffs: amendment gives capacity guarantees and a lower effective unit cost; top-up is flexible and reversible. For your latency target (p95 < 200ms at peak), we need to tune autoscaling and enable prefix/KV caching and dedicated routing to the new pool.

I attached a preliminary quote (Skybound_Dedicated_Renewal_Quote_v4.pdf) with two rows (burst vs amendment) and a proposed SLO table. Can Karthik add a short technical note on throughput assumptions? If procurement wants to proceed with an amendment, I9ll loop in Marissa to approve discounting and legal to issue an amendment.

Next steps:
- Karthik: proposed SLO and recommended config for the 96-GPU amendment
- Alex: preferred billing cadence and whether a PO will be provided

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai

Attachment: Skybound_Dedicated_Renewal_Quote_v4.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Alex Mendoza <alex.mendoza@skyboundlabs.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Skybound Labs Procurement <procurement@skyboundlabs.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-term pool adjustment & renewal questions

Thanks, Soojin.

We9d prefer an amendment to secure capacity — we9re hearing from product that they need predictable throughput for the Q3 launch. Two asks:

1) Can you improve the uplift discount? The quote shows ~12% uplift discount; given the size and the 12-month extension we9d like to see something closer to 15%
2) We experienced a ~5 hour disruption in March that materially impacted a blue-green deploy. Is there room for a one-time credit to make the economics work for this cycle?

We will produce PO if terms are agreeable.

Alex

Attachment: PO_draft_SKY-2027-04.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mendoza <alex.mendoza@skyboundlabs.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-term pool adjustment & renewal questions — technical sizing and SLOs

Alex / Soojin,

Quick technical summary based on the traffic profile:

- Current pool: 64 A100-equivalent GPUs (mixed VMs). Peak concurrent tokens observed: ~5.5k tokens/s.
- Recommended amendment: 96 GPUs to reach target headroom for 8k tokens/s while keeping p95 latency <200ms for typical 512-1k token requests. This assumes:
  * Continuous KV prefix caching enabled for hot prompts
  * Batching window tuned to 10-30ms for high throughput flows
  * Route sticky sessions for the new pool to maintain KV cache locality

SLA/throughput guarantees:
- We can commit to throughput SLOs (p95 latency target) for traffic routed to the reserved pool when the amendment is in place; the SLO is conditional on the routing and cache config above.

Pricing/discount note: if the amendment is executed as a 12-month committed uplift signed by 30-May-2027, we can extend an uplift discount of 15% on the incremental capacity (applied to the uplifted baseline for the duration). That is a limited-time offer due to capacity planning windows.

Attachments: SLA_Tier_Table.xlsx (contains the SLO definitions and credit formulas). I9ve also attached an updated quote with the 15% uplift line item.

Let me know if you want a short architecture call — I can join your SREs to validate the KV cache tuning.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Attachment: SLA_Tier_Table.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Mendoza <alex.mendoza@skyboundlabs.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 14:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-term pool adjustment & renewal questions — pricing approval

Looping in as Soojin requested.

I approve the one-time credit request for the March incident: 2% of the most recent monthly committed invoice as a goodwill credit against the first invoice post-amendment. Approve also the 15% limited-time uplift discount on the incremental capacity, provided Legal signs the standard amendment and billing remains net-30.

Conditions:
- Amendment must include quarterly performance review clause (to validate cache effectiveness and throughput).
- If Skybound later requests region failover or a dedicated control-plane instance, that will be scoped and priced separately.

Soojin: please send final amendment (DocuSign link) with the 96-GPU uplift line, 15% uplift discount on incremental units, the 2% goodwill credit, and net-30 billing. Karthik, please include a short appendix on the cache/routing config to be attached to the amendment.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
